No.

The ruling says that no effect of the card-in-play is applied before contesting.
Sonja's "gain 4" effect is not an effect of her card-in-play. It is an effect
generated by the play of the card.

The "both are removed" is in error. (Reversal)

becomes ready (the contest won) on your next untap phase.

Messages.Author: RocketEddy
Messages.Body:
adam....@gmail.com wrote:
> Wait... how does that work? Someone else has your Sonja blue. You
> bring out your sonja blue, it never hits play because it contests
> right? [you do not gain the 4 pool] The first sonja blue leaves play
> do to contesting and then burns. Next turn you win the contesting and
> the second one comes into play. So why would they both burn?

Somebody else has a copy of Sonja. You *play* (influence out) your
copy, and gain 4 pool. Your copy does not enter play (though it was
still played - for comparison, bleed action cards are played but are
not put in play, i.e. they do not "enter play" either). Their copy of
Sonja burns, but as your copy never entered play it cannot *leave*
play and thus remains unremoved. In your next untap phase, your copy
of Sonja enters play.

HTH :)
Ed.
